message.content:
You are applying a page-entry animation cascade to the SHARED desktop screens of the TaptPay app at /home/runner/workspace.

## Files you own (edit ONLY these two)
- client/src/desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx   (the settings screen, shared by all three verticals)
- client/src/desktop/DesktopLegacyPage.tsx     (wraps a mobile page in a 430px column)

Do NOT edit any other file. In particular do NOT edit client/src/desktop/desktop.css, client/src/App.tsx, client/src/desktop/DesktopShell.tsx, client/src/desktop/DesktopChrome.tsx, or any page under client/src/desktop/pages/ — other agents own those and I own the shared CSS and chrome.

## Context
The tablet/desktop app frame + header + nav are now mounted persistently ABOVE the router, so navigating between screens no longer remounts the chrome. Only the page slot swaps. That means the incoming page's own entry animation IS the page transition. The user's requirement, verbatim: "all componants on every page needs to have a smooth bounce pop in transition with a cascading effect".

## The primitives (already exist in client/src/desktop/desktop.css — read it first, do not modify it)
- `@keyframes desktopBounceIn` — a bounce settle with three decaying overshoots.
- `.dt-rise` — applies desktopBounceIn. Delay = `var(--dt-i, 0) * 52ms + var(--dt-d, 0ms)`.
- `.dt-cascade` — put on a container; auto-assigns `--dt-i` 0..9 to its DIRECT children via nth-child.

Use `.dt-cascade` on a layout container when its direct children are the blocks you want to sequence. Use `.dt-rise` with an explicit `style={{ "--dt-i": 3 } as CSSProperties}` when you need finer control.

## What to change

**DesktopSettingsPage.tsx** — the settings screen is a stack of collapsible sections. Sequence the top-level sections so they cascade in on entry.
IMPORTANT: `.ds-sec-body` currently uses `animation:tileIn` — that fires when a user EXPANDS a section, which is an interaction, not page entry. Leave it alone. You want the section headers/cards themselves to cascade on entry, not their expanded bodies.

**DesktopLegacyPage.tsx** — this renders `.tapt-desktop-legacy-wrap > .tapt-desktop-legacy-column` with a mobile page inside. It currently has no entry animation at all. Give the column a single `.dt-rise` entry so it bounces in like every other screen rather than hard-cutting. Do not try to cascade the mobile page's internals — that markup belongs to the mobile app and must not be touched.

Rules:
1. ONLY animate what plays when the SCREEN FIRST APPEARS. Leave anything driven by an in-page state change alone.
2. Do not change layout, geometry, spacing, colors, copy, or behaviour. Animation only.
3. Do not add any animation library. No framer-motion. CSS only — this is an explicit project rule.
4. Do not add a `prefers-reduced-motion` block; desktop.css already neutralises all animation inside `.tapt-desktop-viewport` globally.
5. Keep the cascade snappy: the last element should start no later than ~450ms. Settings has many sections — group or cap them so the tail does not drag.
6. Settings writes real merchant configuration. Do not touch any query, mutation, handler, or state logic. Note there is a test at client/src/desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.test.tsx — read it first and make sure your change cannot break it.

## Verify before reporting
For each file you changed, run a syntax check:
  cd /home/runner/workspace && npx esbuild <file> --loader=tsx --outfile=/dev/null
Both must pass. Do NOT run `npx tsc` (project-wide, slow, and I run it centrally).

## Report back
A concise list: per file, what you sequenced and in what order, and anything you deliberately left alone (with the reason). Flag anything that looked like a pre-existing bug — do not fix it.

content.text:
Done. Both files changed, animation only.

## `client/src/desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx`

Two `.dt-cascade` containers, plus one line of local CSS to offset the second column:

- **`.ds-left`** (added `dt-cascade`) — its 6 direct children sequence in order: identity row (avatar + status pill) → business name → `SETTINGS` kicker → Customer Payment Page button → the 3-up vertical mode grid → Log Out. Steps 0–5, so 0–260ms.
- **`.ds-right`** (added `dt-cascade`) — its 6 direct children sequence: Payment Board Builder card → Business Details → Dashboard Preferences → Subscription & Billing → Account → Transaction Notifications. Steps 0–5 with `--dt-d: 80ms` so the right column reads as following the left rather than racing it.
- **New CSS rule** `.ds-right.dt-cascade { --dt-d: 80ms; }` added to the component's own `DS_CSS` template (I did not touch `desktop.css`). Last element starts at 5×52ms + 80ms = **340ms**, inside the ~450ms budget. `--dt-d` inherits down to the cascade children; `--dt-i` still comes from the shared nth-child rules.

Deliberately left alone:
- **`.ds-sec-body` / `animation: tileIn`** — as instructed. It fires on expand, which is an interaction. Untouched. Note the collapsed sections' bodies are conditionally rendered (`{open && …}`), so animating them on entry would have been wrong anyway.
- **The `.ds-modes` three mode buttons, notification rows, billing rows, team list, billing history** — all either inside an expanded body (interaction-driven) or nested below the top-level blocks. They rise as part of their parent block; no sub-cascade added.
- **No query/mutation/handler/state change.** The only diffs are two `className` strings and one CSS rule.

## `client/src/desktop/DesktopLegacyPage.tsx`

- Added `dt-rise` to `.tapt-desktop-legacy-column` (no `--dt-i`, so it fires at 0ms — a single bounce for the whole 430px column instead of the previous hard cut).
- Did **not** cascade the wrapped mobile page's internals; that markup belongs to the mobile app.

## Verification

- `npx esbuild … --outfile=/dev/null` passes for both files. (Note: `--loader=tsx` errors with "loader without extension only applies when reading from stdin"; the working form for a file path is `--loader:.tsx=tsx`.)
- I also ran `npx jest client/src/desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.test.tsx` — **9/9 pass**. Nothing in that test queries by class, and jsdom does not evaluate animations, so the change is inert to it.

## Flagged, not fixed

- `.dt-rise` / `.dt-cascade > *` set `opacity: 0` and rely on the animation to reveal. The reduced-motion block in `desktop.css` (line 495) clamps `animation-duration` to `1ms` rather than disabling the animation, so reveal still happens there — fine. But if these classes are ever applied outside `.tapt-desktop-viewport`, or the keyframes fail to load, the element stays invisible. Pre-existing property of the shared primitive, which you own; noting only.
- `.tapt-desktop-legacy-column` is an `overflow-y: auto` scroll container and now animates `transform`. Harmless once the 0.54s animation completes, but during it the column establishes a containing block. No visual issue expected at a 0ms delay; raising it as the one interaction between my change and existing geometry.
